newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop soymeal down, soyoil off on acreage.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop soymeal down, soyoil off on acreage.

text.p: CBOT new crop soymeal futures were down half the $10 per ton daily limit on surprisingly high USDA 1997 planted soybean acreage figures but old crop was higher on ideas of tight stocks, traders said.
Soyoil prices were lower across the board.
USDA on Monday put 1997 soybean plantings at 68.8 million acres, the highest since 1980 and well above trade expectations for 65.85 million.
But old crop contracts held firm on ideas lower-than-expected quarterly stocks figures would lead to dangerously tight ending stocks.
USDA put soybean quarterly stocks at 1.078 billion bushels, below trade expectations for 1.093 billion.
At 1125 CST, soymeal was down $5.50 per ton to up $1.00 with December down $5.50 at $218.00 and May up $1.00 at $283.70. Soyoil was down 0.63 to 0.45 cent per lb with May down 0.45 at 23.97.

USDA analysts said the surge in soybean acreage to the highest level since 1980, was aided by larger plantings in "fringe" areas. North Dakota's expected planted acreage was up 35 percent, or 250,000 acres, for a total of 1.15 million acres of soybeans.
Bulls pointed to ideas acreage figures were not set in stone because most farmers had not yet begun planting and wet weather had delayed pesticide applications in some areas.
"Farmers can change acreage and they will do so depending on weather," said Terry Francl, senior economist with the American Farm Bureau Federation.

One analyst said using USDA's soybean acreage figures and six-year average yields, next year's soybean crop would reach 2.477 billion bushels. But the analyst also noted this year's demand for soybeans was 2.431 billion bushels, meaning 1997-98 ending stocks would remain tight.
